cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, which is the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here is about sweep TIMING and not about the defect. That must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: a bytestream reader kept the old base of a buffer that had been reallocated
object: tile->packed_headers, grown by av_realloc, with a GetByteContext holding the old base
lifetime_ender: av_realloc(tile->packed_headers, ...), which frees the old block when it moves
shape: a saved reader context holding a base pointer that realloc invalidated
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, with no pool or refstruct layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is `s->g = tile->packed_headers_stream`, then reads through that context.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/jpeg2000dec.c zeroes the context with `memset(&tile->packed_headers_stream, 0, sizeof(tile->packed_headers_stream));` after the realloc. That memset is absent at 4b2248594c7f^.
nested_why: the object came straight from av_malloc/av_mallocz/av_malloc_array/av_realloc -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool, AVRefStructPool or other recycling layer between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../pool-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: what dangles is not a bare pointer but a whole READER CONTEXT -- a struct of pointers into the old block -- which is why the fix zeroes the struct rather than rebasing one field. A reader re-created from the new base would be correct; one carrying the old base passes its own bounds checks while reading freed storage, so the context's internal consistency is exactly what hides the defect.
